The dragon did not move.

Neither did I.

That seemed fair for the first few seconds.

Then it became his choice.

I had just told a creature older than my kingdom that the future he remembered me not being part of had happened with me in it once already.

There were several reasonable responses to that.

Disbelief.

Questions.

Eating me.

I had prepared for two of those.

Ithar stared.

I shifted my weight off the bad leg.

The movement was small.

His eye followed it anyway.

Eventually he said, “Not this time.”

“Yes.”

“You chose those words.”

“I did.”

“Why?”

“Because they were short.”

His nostril opened.

Not quite a sigh.

I had started assigning meanings to the nostrils.

That was probably dangerous.

“Say what you mean without protecting it with brevity.”

I looked at him.

“That sounds expensive.”

“I have not charged you.”

“Yet.”

“Greg.”

That was the first time my name sounded different in his mouth.

Not important.

Not friendly.

Placed.
